problem.text: The change attempts a temporary workaround for a CUDA dependency error by pinning nvidia-persistenced before Linux toolkit installation.

reasoning.text: Placing the preference before the existing network-based CUDA installer would make package selection policy available before installation, rather than changing CUDA compilation or Python dependencies.

impact.text: The new condition targets the four Ubuntu CUDA matrix rows, excluding Windows and the CUDA-empty packaging row. However, malformed indentation appears to prevent the workflow from being accepted at all.

source_notes.text: The introduction and merge entries were read. They establish the inherited manual build matrix, PowerShell command default and opt-in release publication; neither records a defect directly affected by this pin.

Issue #2, “Error: setup script specifies an absolute path,” reports a wheel-build failure involving setup.py paths. Its reported error differs from this change's package-selection workaround; the issue does not establish the CUDA dependency diagnosis.

Whole-parent searches found no nvidia-persistenced or apt-get occurrences. A broader CUDA search also found documentation, calibration text and native code, but was truncated; those occurrences do not independently identify this dependency failure.

limitations: No YAML parser, GitHub Actions job, PowerShell command or APT installation was executed. The indentation check only measured a transcription of the added text.
The linked NVIDIA forum was unavailable through approved evidence. Package availability, the dependency conflict and the precise APT semantics of priority 1001 remain unverified.

claims.text: The added step intends to write an APT preference for Package: nvidia-persistenced, version 570.148.08-1ubuntu1, priority 1001, to /etc/apt/preferences.d/99-nvidia-persistenced, then refresh package indexes. It does not explicitly install that package.

The existing next step invokes Jimver/cuda-toolkit@v0.2.24 with CUDA 12.8.1, network installation and --toolkit. Both steps use the same non-Windows, nonempty-CUDA condition. The workflow retains its default pwsh shell.
The workaround trades unrestricted package selection for one hard-coded distribution version. Its comment calls this temporary, but the source supplies no fallback or package-availability check.

A standard-library Python transcription measured indentation of 10, 0, 0 and 10 spaces for the four command lines. This confirms the textual indentation discrepancy, not YAML parsing or installer behavior.

findings.description: The added multiline command contains two unindented lines that escape the YAML run block, apparently invalidating the workflow before its conditional steps can run.
findings.trigger: GitHub Actions loads the modified build.yml workflow.
findings.expected_behavior: All lines of the preference-writing command remain inside the run scalar, allowing the workflow to schedule its jobs.
findings.actual_behavior: Pin: and Pin-Priority: begin at column zero, ending the indented run scalar; the following indented apt-get command does not restore the intended workflow structure. The suspected reach is the entire workflow, not only Linux CUDA jobs.

verification.description: Compared the new run block with the enclosing workflow indentation and inherited job structure.
verification.limits: No YAML parser or Actions validation was run.

verification.description: Counted leading spaces in the four added command lines.
verification.limits: Text measurement only; not execution of the repository workflow.

annotation.summary: Attempts to pin nvidia-persistenced before Linux CUDA installation, but unindented command lines appear to invalidate the workflow; dependency resolution remains untested.

argv:
s="          echo 'Package: nvidia-persistenced
Pin: version 570.148.08-1ubuntu1
Pin-Priority: 1001' | sudo tee /etc/apt/preferences.d/99-nvidia-persistenced
          sudo apt-get update"; print([(x.lstrip().split(':')[0],len(x)-len(x.lstrip())) for x in s.splitlines()])
